fact: The Ministry of Lands is reviewing LIMS workflows and developing digital procedures to move the remaining manual land transactions onto the platform.
Malawi launched LIMS in February 2024, a web-based system linking Lands, Surveys and Physical Planning where registered users can view land parcels and assets.
Registered LIMS users can submit documents, receive notifications and make payments, including ground rent and application fees.

The Ministry of Lands, with the World Bank's AGCOM project, is implementing the Land Information Management System, with a contract signed 10 May 2021 for a 20-month rollout including data capture and go-live phases.
Lands Minister Chimwemwe Chipungu said the ministry's Land Information Management System, holding title deeds and other land data, was hacked about two weeks before 2026-10-27.
Malawi's Minister of Lands said that LIMS has replaced manual, fire-prone records and enables Malawians to access land information digitally, as registrars were trained to operate it.

Malawi's Lands Minister said in an interview that the ministry holds its land records in a Land Information Management System, against which a land audit checks physical files, and that it commissioned the new K965 million Ntchisi Land Registry.

Lands Minister Chimwemwe Chipungu said on 12 August 2026 that the ministry is currently digitising land administration processes via a Land Information Management System (LIMS), and an audit matched paper files against records in LIMS.
247Malawi reports the Ministry of Lands launched the Land Information Management System (LIMS) for land management in Blantyre, to replace paper documents in tracking land transactions.
